A man's recitation reminded the Prophet of verses he had been made to forget; keep refreshing the Quran, which escapes faster than hobbled camels, and never say 'I forgot it'.
Allah listens to nothing as He listens to a prophet reciting the Quran in a sweet voice, and Abu Musa was given a voice like those of David's family.
In the year of the Conquest of Mecca the Prophet recited Surat al-Fath on his mount while travelling, repeating the words, as Ibn Mughaffal later demonstrated.
A cloud that frightened a horse while its owner recited al-Kahf was tranquillity descending, and the canopy of lamps over Usaid b. Hudair as he recited was angels listening.
A believer who recites the Quran is like a sweet, fragrant orange; the proficient reciter is with the noble recording angels, and one who falters in it has two rewards.
Allah commanded the Prophet to recite to Ubayy, who wept at being named; the Prophet asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him and wept at a verse of Surat al-Nisa'.
In Hims Ibn Mas'ud recited Surah Yusuf, which the Prophet had approved; the man who denied it smelled of wine, so Ibn Mas'ud lashed him with the prescribed punishment.
Three verses recited in prayer, or verses taught or recited in the mosque each morning, are better than as many large she-camels.
The Quran will intercede for its reciters on Resurrection Day, and al-Baqara and Al Imran will come like two clouds or flocks of birds pleading for those who recited them.
An angel announced to the Prophet two lights given to no prophet before, the Fatiha and the end of al-Baqara, whose last two verses suffice whoever recites them at night.
Whoever learns by heart ten verses of Surah al-Kahf, from its beginning or, in one narration, its end, will be protected from the Dajjal.
'Say: He is Allah, One' equals a third of the Quran, and Allah loves the expedition leader who ended his recitation in prayer with it because it describes the Compassionate.
The Prophet said verses unlike any seen before had come down: the Mu'awwadhatain, 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the dawn' and 'with the Lord of men'.
Umar and Ubayy objected to others' different recitations, but the Prophet approved each, saying the Quran was sent down in seven modes, granted at his request to ease his people.
Ibn Mas'ud told a man who recited all the mufassal surahs in one rak'ah that he rushed like poetry, recalling how the Prophet paired surahs, two in each rak'ah.
The Prophet read 'muddakir' with a d, and Abu Darda' heard him recite 'By the night when it covers' with 'the male and the female', as Ibn Mas'ud did.
Ibn Mas'ud recited seventy-plus surahs before the Prophet, who named him, Salim, Ubayy and Mu'adh as Quran teachers; four Ansar collected it, and Allah ordered it recited to Ubayy.
